newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Dlr/mark rises, most European bourses gain.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Dlr/mark rises, most European bourses gain.

text.p: The dollar continued climbing against the mark on Tuesday afternoon despite comments from German central bank chief economist Otmar Issing that the mark's exchange rate was one of the most important indicators in setting monetary policy.
Though his remarks initially sounded mark supportive, they were tempered by his other comment that there was not an automatic link between the dollar/mark rate and German interest rate policies.

In equities, most European stock markets shrugged off a weaker Wall Street open to advance amid solid corporate earnings and expectations the strong dollar will help make European goods cheaper abroad and boost exports.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average was down 24.15 points at 8,174.30 in mid-afternoon.

"Stocks like a decent economy," said Pierre Ellis, senior economist at Primark Decision Economics in the U.S. "Now that long-term interest rates have backed up, it will dampen some of the enthusiasm in the stock market."
Benchmark 30-year U.S. bond prices started lower, pushing the yield up to 6.49 percent, before the first leg of the Treasury's three-part quarterly refunding.
The Treasury will sell $16.0 billion in three-year notes on Tuesday, $12.0 billion in 10-year notes on Wednesday and $10.0 billion in 30-year bonds on Thursday.

Issing said in an interview with "Boerse-Online" magazine: "after money supply, the exchange rate is one of the most important indicators for the Bundesbank. The fact that the mark has weakened so fast and so significantly certainly gives us something to think about."
He said it was not necessarily the mark's level but the speed of its depreciation that worried the Bundesbank.

"These comments that are coming out are trying to make some effort to stop it (the dollar's gains against the mark) but short of intervening, I don't think it's going to work," said James Powers, vice-president at Westdeutsche Landesbank Girozentrale in New York.
The dollar buying spree started in the morning on relief that Germany's central bank had stuck to its planned, fixed 3.0-percent weekly money market operation.

Some traders had speculated the Bundesbank would surprise the market and also announce a variable-rate operation to allow rates to drift up and lift the mark from near eight-year lows versus the dollar.

Analysts said the market was now aiming to push the dollar up to 1.90 marks, especially if German jobs data on Wednesday shows little improvement in cutting joblessness. The dollar's last visit above 1.90 marks was in October 1989 when it peaked at 1.9221 marks.
A clearer path for the dollar to rise against the mark calmed Germany's stock market, which shed about two percent on Monday because of German interest rate jitters.
Germany's DAX index closed bourse trading up 5.74 points at 4,302.68, with the highest turnover seen in banking shares as merger speculation lingered.

But Paris traders were not yet convinced German rate threats were gone. The blue-chip CAC-40 index slipped after Germany's Ifo economic research institute said the Bundesbank might send a signal to currency markets if the dollar rose above 1.90 marks.
"I could imagine that a dollar above 1.90 marks would set alarm bells ringing in Frankfurt," said Ifo economist Willi Leibfritz.
London shares also suffered rate worries before the Bank of England 's monetary policy-setting meeting on Wednesday and Thursday.
"I'm afraid that the uncertainty about interest rates will keep volumes low and markets volatile," a dealer said.
But until then, London traders said corporate earnings were driving the market higher. The FTSE jumped more than one percent, led by the oil and drug sectors.
British Petroleum Co Plc hit a year high and said it planned to buy back shares from "time to time."
BAA Plc jumped after the airport management group said pre-tax profits for the three months ending June 30 rose in line with analysts' forecasts.
In the afternoon, BAA shares were up 18-1/2 pence at 580, just off its session high of 582.
But National Westminster Bank shares tumbled after earnings failed to meet analysts' expectations.
Natwest shares were down 36 pence at 835, off its session low of 818.7.
CURRENCIES AT 1420 GMT
The dollar was at 1.8794 marks and 119.15 yen, compared to 1.8635 and 118.40 in late trading on Monday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1420 GMT
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index was up 54.8points at 4,950.50
FRANKFURT - The DAX index ended up 5.74 points at 4,302.68 in bourse trade. The IBIS DAX was up 14.11 points at 4,316.61 in electronic trading.
PARIS - The CAC-40 was down 10.16 points at 2,982.25.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold was fixed in the morning in London at $323.35, down from London's close at $323.65 on Monday. ($ = 0.613 British Pounds)
